g.data-info: Fragments of old osteons left between newer ones after bone has been remodelled.
The basic structural unit of compact bone: a cylinder of concentric lamellae around a central canal, bounded by a cement line.
Rings of calcified matrix laid down around the Haversian canal, giving the bone strength.
Tiny channels linking lacunae to each other and to the canal, so nutrients and wastes can pass between osteocytes.
A small space between the lamellae that houses an osteocyte.
A mature bone cell trapped in a lacuna that maintains the surrounding bone matrix.
A channel running at right angles to the Haversian canals that links them to each other and to the bone surface.
The central canal of an osteon carrying blood vessels and nerves along the bone.
